bites.headline: Why study Financial Markets (2008)?
bites.body: Financial institutions are a pillar of civilized society, supporting people in their productive ventures and managing the economic risks they take on.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: What’s at stake
bites.body: The workings of these institutions are important to comprehend if we are to predict their actions today and their evolution in the coming information age.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Finance and Insurance as Powerful Forces in Our Economy and Society
bites.body: Professor Shiller provides a description of the course, Financial Markets, including administrative details and the topics to be discussed in each lecture.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Professor
bites.body: He briefly discusses the importance of studying finance and each key topic.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Lecture topics will include: behavioral finance, financial technology, financial instruments, commercial banking, investment banking, financial markets and institutions, real estate, regulation, monetary policy, and democratization of…
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: The Universal Principle of Risk Management: Pooling and the Hedging of Risks
bites.body: Statistics and mathematics underlie the theories of finance.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Statistics
bites.body: Probability Theory and various distribution types are important to understanding finance.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Financial analysis methods such as present values and valuing streams of payments are fundamental to understanding the time value of money and have been in practice for centuries.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Technology and Invention in Finance
bites.body: Technology and innovation underlie finance.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Technology
bites.body: In order to manage risks successfully, particularly long-term, we must pool large amounts of risk among many, diverse people and overcome barriers such as moral hazard and erroneous framing.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: The tax and welfare system is one of the most important risk management systems.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Portfolio Diversification and Supporting Financial Institutions (CAPM Model)
bites.body: Portfolio diversification is the most fundamental concept of risk management.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Portfolio
bites.body: The allocation of financial resources in stocks, bonds, riskless, assets, oil and other assets determine the expected return and risk of a portfolio.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: An important mission of financial institutions is to provide portfolio-diversification services.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Insurance: The Archetypal Risk Management Institution
bites.body: Insurance provides significant risk management to a broad public, and is an essential tool for promoting human welfare.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Institution
bites.body: By pooling large numbers of independent or low-correlated risks, insurance providers can minimize overall risk.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Innovation and government regulation have played important roles in the formation and oversight of insurance institutions.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Efficient Markets vs. Excess Volatility
bites.body: Several theories in finance relate to stock price analysis and prediction.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Volatility
bites.body: The efficient markets hypothesis states that stock prices for publicly-traded companies reflect all available information.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: These tests show that efficient markets theory is a half-truth: it is difficult but not impossible for some people to beat the market.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Behavioral Finance: The Role of Psychology
bites.body: Behavioral Finance is a relatively recent revolution in finance that applies insights from all of the social sciences to finance.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Behavioral
bites.body: New decision-making models incorporate psychology and sociology, among other disciplines, to explain economic and financial phenomenon, such as erratic stock price variations.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: Kahneman and Tversky's Prospect Theory addresses such issues and sheds light on irrational deviations from traditional decision-making models.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Human Foibles, Fraud, Manipulation, and Regulation
bites.body: Regulation of financial and securities markets is intended to protect investors while still enabling them to make personal investment decisions.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Manipulation
bites.body: Psychological phenomena, such as magical thinking, overconfidence, and representativeness heuristic can cause deviations from rational behavior and distort financial decision-making.
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA

bites.headline: Carry this forward
bites.body: However, regulation and regulatory bodies, such as the SEC, FDIC, and SIPC, most of which were created just after the Great Depression, are intended to help prevent the manipulation of investors' psychological foibles and maintain trust…
bites.attribution_line: Robert J. Shiller, Financial Markets (2008) (Yale University: Open Yale Courses), https://oyc.yale.edu/economics/econ-252-08 (Accessed September 23, 2026). License: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA
